text:
alex: Heads-up — we've seen 99.9th spikes on small interactive routes. Suspect batching window + a few slow workers. Thinking about hedging before a request is entered into a long batch. ideas?

sarah: yeah, hedging seems like low-hanging. but batch windowing complicates it — if we hedge after window closes we duplicate work. we should hedge while requests are still queued, not after batch dispatch. :thinking:

mz: agree. also idempotency. if we allow duplicate execution we need a hedged-request id so runtime can dedupe or cancel early. otherwise logs/metrics double-count.

jamie: rough config idea (per-route):
```
hedging: {
  enabled: true,
  hedge_after_ms: 20,
  max_hedges: 1,
  apply_while_queued: true,
  share_kv_key: true
}
batching: {
  window_ms: 10
}
```
this makes hedges fire during queue window, not post-dispatch.

sarah: streaming note: once we start streaming tokens, you can't meaningfully hedge mid-stream. hedging only for pre-dispatch or pre-first-token scenarios.

alex: OK. what's the cost tradeoff? double GPU work vs tail reduction? need guardrails.

mz: add quotas + cost buckets. also prefer hedging to cheaper variants (quantized/shorter context) where possible. header: `X-Hedge-Variant: fallback-small`

infra-bot: Created metric `gateway.hedge.attempts` and `gateway.hedge.success_latency_reduction`.

jamie: runtime needs a cancel path: when the first model starts streaming, edge sends `cancel-hedge:<hedge_id>` to any in-flight duplicates. must be lightweight.

sarah: for KV/cache duplication: if `share_kv_key=true` the hedged requests reuse same cache key so early compute benefits both. runtime needs to publish a small shared-result token.

mz: rollout plan: feature-flag, 1% of traffic -> measure p99, cost delta, failed hedges. if p99 improves ~> keep expanding.

alex: action items: (1) jamie - prototype header + cancel signal wire format, (2) mz - idempotency semantics doc + metrics, (3) sarah - update batching/hedge config schema + canary plan. will sync in 48h. :thumbsup:

sarah: one more: document the interaction with ingress backpressure. hedging should not defeat admission control. hedges must respect admission quotas or they amplify overload.

alex: good call. add to tasks.

jamie: logging snippets we'll need: `hedge_id`, `route`, `hedge_origin` (queue|timer), `cancel_signal_sent`. small and indexable.

mz: also add test case: high-queue scenario where hedge_after_ms < window_ms and verify single response delivered and duplicates canceled.

alex: thanks all — pulling this into an RFC follow-up doc after the sync.
